mathematical_checks.reasoning: S=2^j is positive. H=min(T,S) is positive for T>0 and satisfies H<=T and H<=S. X=max(A,S)+kH is at least S, hence H<=X. No circular window-size hypothesis is assumed.

For n in Icc A B and its shell [S,2S), let X0=max(A,S). Then X0<=n, n<=X0+T and n<X0+S. If T<=S, the first bound puts n in [X0,X0+T] and T>0 puts its closed upper endpoint into the k=1 half-open window. If S<=T, n lies in the k=0 window. Thus the B=A+T endpoint is retained rather than dropped. An endpoint at a dyadic boundary is assigned to its next legal shell by j=Nat.log 2 n.
The global cover is explicitly for n>0, and largeSource excludes zero. Empty Icc intervals produce no source obligations. No theorem claims that zero is in a positive dyadic shell.

An active shell is filtered by an existential witness in the actual original Icc A B, positive and above the retained threshold. The witness theorem retains membership, positivity, threshold and both shell bounds; activity is not inferred merely from a formal shell label.

Pointwise coverage supplies at least one window occurrence. All F(n) are assumed nonnegative, including the additional window points. Repeated coverage across windows or shells is therefore valid for an upper bound. The theorem asserts neither disjointness nor equality.

The natural half-open interval has exactly H points. Eight windows cost 8H<=8T, and the active set is a subset of range(log_2 B+1). The total bound 8T(log_2 B+1) follows without an unstated disjointness assumption.

For A<=B, B!=0, j<=log_2 B and k<8, both max(A,S) and H are <=B; hence X<=B+7B=8B. For x>=8 and B<=x^K this gives X<=x^(K+1). The bound concerns window starts, as required by the caller; H<=X is supplied separately.

The exact factorization f=g*fp, g>0, and f<=L*x^(-delta) yield fp*x^delta<=L/g. With the retained real point R=fp*x^(delta/2)<=n<2S and T>=L/g, both T and S dominate R/16. Their minimum does too. No shifted-divisor estimate is assumed in this elementary argument.

For alpha=delta/(16P), the stated delta>0, delta<=1 and P>=1 give 0<alpha<1/2. X<=x^P gives X^alpha<=x^(delta/16). The strict margin 16<x^(7delta/16), fp>=1 and H>=fp*x^(delta/2)/16 imply X^alpha<=H and fp*H^alpha<H, hence fp<H^(1-alpha). The strict modulus inequality is not weakened to a non-strict one.

The actual retained source point and n<2S<=2X give the lower bound on X needed for the Shiu threshold and logarithm. The required fixed margins and threshold remain explicit hypotheses. A shell index alone is not substituted for those conditions.

The positive constant and threshold precede forall X,H,q,b. X>=X0, H>0, q>0, X^kappa<=H, H<=X, strict q<H^(1-alpha), and q.Coprime b are all retained. The displayed exponential prime-reciprocal RHS is preserved. The window theorem substitutes its actual X,H into this supplied bound and does not establish the analytic theorem itself.

manuscript.assessment: The manuscript explicitly calls for sign splitting, dyadic shells, and lengths comparable to min(shell scale,L/g). The new finite natural-interval subdivision supplies that elementary step. With Q=L/g>=1 and T=ceil Q, the preserved ceiling lemma gives Q<=T<=2Q, so min(Q,S)<=min(T,S)<=2min(Q,S). The actual quotient-to-natural-endpoint instantiation is not assembled in these modules. No substantive manuscript gap was identified for the elementary subdivision itself.
